title: The First 90 Days as a Leader

parts.visual:
Your first 90 days in a new executive role define your tenure. The goal is to learn rapidly, establish trust, and secure 'early wins'.

The 3 Phases:
1. Days 1-30: Listen and Learn (Do not change anything major yet).
2. Days 31-60: Assess and Align (Build alliances and identify quick fixes).
3. Days 61-90: Execute Early Wins (Deliver visible value).
parts.audio: Your first 90 days define your tenure. Phase 1: Listen. Phase 2: Assess. Phase 3: Execute early wins to establish credibility.

questions.question: It is your first week as VP. You notice a flawed process. What should you do?
options: Tear the process down immediately and implement the system you used at your old job.
Note the flaw, but take the time to understand *why* the process exists before trying to change it.
Fire the person who created it.
questions.correct_answer: Note the flaw, but take the time to understand *why* the process exists before trying to change it.
questions.explanation: Chesterton's Fence principle: Do not remove a fence until you know why it was put up in the first place.

questions.question: Listen to the new executive. What phase of the 90 days is she in?
questions.tts_text: My goal this month is to hold 1-on-1s with every team member just to understand their daily challenges.
questions.explanation: Information gathering and relationship building are the absolute priorities of the first 30 days.

questions.question: What is an 'Early Win'?
options: A quick, visible, and successful project that builds your credibility and creates momentum for larger changes.
questions.correct_answer: A quick, visible, and successful project that builds your credibility and creates momentum for larger changes.
questions.explanation: Early wins prove to your team and your boss that hiring you was the right decision.

questions.question: Which behavior is toxic for a new leader entering an established team?
options: Constantly saying 'At my old company, we did it this way...'
questions.correct_answer: Constantly saying 'At my old company, we did it this way...'
questions.explanation: This alienates the new team. You were hired to lead *this* company, not recreate your old one.
